Hi team / Mike,

Draft summary attached — redwood_kms_key_ceremony_summary.pdf — plus aCSV that lays out our rotation windows redwood_kms_rotation_schedule.csv. Quick highlights (extracted from the attached):

1) Architecture overview (in transit & at rest)- All customer data in transit is protected using TLS 1.3 (AES-GCM) with ephemeral keys. We enforce strong cipher suites and forward secrecy; TLS termination is only at edge proxies in our VPC.

2) At-rest envelope encryption- Data encrypted at rest uses envelope encryption: each tenant/data-object has a unique data encryption key (DEK) generated by the service. DEKs are encrypted (wrapped) by a Customer-tenant master key (CMK) stored in a cloud KMS. The CMK is backed by an HSM-rooted key (HSM-backed key); HSM vendor and model are included in the redacted attestation.

3) KMS & HSM details- We operate a managed KMS with optional BYOK (customer bring-your-own-key). Our default is Redwood-managed CMKs protected by HSM-held root keys (FIPS-140-2/3 compliant modules). For BYOK, key import is performed via a secure import ceremony using split knowledge and temporary import tokens; imported keys are opaque to Redwood and marked non-exportable.

4) Key ceremony and governance- Key generation for root/wrapping keys happens in HSMs under dual control with recorded key ceremony logs. We maintain a documented key-ceremony playbook: roles (crypto-op lead, auditor), quorum rules, step-by-step attestation checklists, and tamper-evident logs. We rotate wrapping keys on a configurable cadence (default 90 days) and perform an annual cryptoperiod review. Old wrapping keys are retired and kept for decryption-only for a 180-day overlap period to support rollback and object recovery.

5) Rotation, rollback & testing- Rotations are staged (canary -> rollout) and include automated test vectors to validate decryption of existing artifacts. We perform dry-run rotation tests quarterly in an isolated environment. In the event of a failed rotation, the system falls back to the previous wrapping key; rollback is tested as part of each dry-run.

6) Logging & retention- KMS and HSM event logs are forwarded to our audit logging pipeline (immutable storage) with 400+ days retention for cryptographic operations and admin actions. Access to keys and ceremony logs is restricted and audited.

7) Evidence & certifications- Attached is a redacted HSM attestation (redwood_hsm_attestation_redacted.pdf). Our HSM vendor holds relevant certifications (FIPS, Common Criteria) which are noted in the attestation. Also linking our SOC 2 page in case you need the report.

Notes on BYOK: the import ceremony generates an import-wrapped key that is never exportable. Customers may request deletion; deletion requests are logged and require multi-party approval.

Please review the two attachments; Alex — confirmed the attestation can be redacted/sanitized for external sharing (vendor ok). Mike — let me know if you'd like more granular logs or a sanitized excerpt from the ceremony logs.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Security Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
